title: What If a Jellyfish Swarm Shut Down a Nuclear Reactor?

scenes.text: What if jellyfish shut down a nuclear reactor? It already happened.
In 2013, a swarm of moon jellyfish entered the cooling water inlet at Oskarshamn in Sweden.
They blocked the pipes that cool Unit 3, a 1,400 megawatt reactor supplying about 5 percent of Sweden's electricity.
Operators shut the unit down. Within about two days the intake was cleared and the restart began.
It was not the first time. The same plant lost Unit 1 in 2005, and California's Diablo Canyon lost a unit in 2008.
In 2011, a jellyfish invasion in Florida clogged a plant's intakes and killed about five tons of fish. A soft, brainless animal beat a reactor.
